A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same MatPedia research, with corresponding sections, equations, eight figures and four tables. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of text-to-material generation, image-to-material generation and material decomposition, plus decoder fine-tuning and hybrid-training ablations in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative evaluations, ablations and qualitative material-generation results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–8.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the joint RGB-PBR encoding, decoder fine-tuning, DiT backbone, task-specific LoRAs and rectified-flow objective. The added related-work comparison describes the existing architecture without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MatHybrid-410K with the same RGB and PBR subsets and the same stated MaterialPicker test set. The three material tasks and point-light illumination scenario are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: MatFuse quantitatively and ControlMat/MaterialPicker qualitatively for text-to-material generation; MatFuse and Material Palette for image-to-material generation; Material Palette and RGB↔X for decomposition. Newly cited IntrinsiX and PhotoMat are not added to the reported evaluations.

E3.justification: The reported data counts, test set, metrics, 1024×1024 resolution, 10K-step decoder training, 200K-step DiT training and 50-step inference remain unchanged. Hardware disclosures are removed, but no changed experimental procedure is reported.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 retains the same decoder fine-tuning ablation, hybrid-training comparison and point-light generalization analysis, supported by the same Tables 1 and 4 and Figures 7–8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the reported experiments. No statistical reporting procedure is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and rankings in Tables 1–4 and qualitative examples in Figures 4–8 are retained. For example, Table 1 reports MatPedia CLIP 0.283 and DINO-FID 1.31, versus MatFuse 0.261 and 1.90, in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 3's definitions and Section 4's encoding, decoding and loss equations (1–4) retain the same mathematical content. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about the joint RGB-PBR representation, unified support for three tasks, MatHybrid-410K and native 1024×1024 generation. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of RGB-PBR complementarity, hybrid-training benefits and point-light generalization are retained. Section 6 preserves the limitation concerning tileable generation through noise rolling and the proposed extension to height and subsurface-scattering channels.

D1.justification: Section 4.5 removes v1's disclosures that decoder and DiT training each use 32 H20 GPUs and that 20-second inference runs on a single H20 GPU. Other hyperparameters and the timing value remain, so this reduces reproducibility information without establishing an actual hardware change.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds IntrinsiX, called 'IntrinsicX' in the prose, and contrasts its per-channel LoRAs with MatPedia's per-task LoRAs on a shared latent space. PhotoMat is also added to the GAN-related citations, expanding the bibliography from 58 to 60 works.

P1.justification: v2 makes a short related-work addition, adds an acknowledgment and funding paragraph, corrects 'NanKai' to 'Nankai', and makes limited local text edits. The main section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained with layout adjustments. Figure 3 moves between columns on page 5, Table 1 moves from page 6 to page 5, and Table 2 moves from page 7 to page 6; spacing and subsequent text flow also change.

improvement.justification: The added IntrinsiX comparison and PhotoMat citation modestly improve research positioning. However, removing the training GPU specifications and the hardware basis for the retained 20-second inference claim weakens reproducibility and timing interpretability. This concrete loss outweighs the limited literature improvement, while the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
